_comment: Python rules. Extracted from the v0.12 python templates, with the rationale that was previously implicit and the checks that previously lived in analyze/SKILL.md's pattern library.

rules.title: Type hints everywhere
rules.statement: **Type hints everywhere.** Use modern syntax: `list[int]`, `dict[str, X]`, `X | None`.
rules.rationale: Hints are the only machine-checkable documentation of intent a Python codebase has. Without them a refactor is a search-and-hope exercise, and tools like mypy have nothing to check.

check.reason: coverage of hints is mypy's job, not a grep's

rules.title: Prefer module-level functions over deep class hierarchies
rules.statement: **Module-level functions over deep class hierarchies.** Prefer composition.
rules.rationale: Inheritance couples subclasses to a base's internals, and each level makes behaviour harder to locate. A module function is directly testable and has no hidden state from three classes up.

check.reason: depth thresholds produce more false positives than value

rules.title: No wildcard imports
rules.rationale: A wildcard import makes the origin of every name unknowable without running the code, silently shadows locals when the upstream module adds a name, and defeats every static tool that resolves references.

rules.title: Docstrings on public functions
rules.statement: **Docstrings for public functions** — one-line summary, blank line, body if needed.
rules.rationale: A public function's contract lives in someone's head until it is written down. The one-line summary is what shows up in editors and generated docs, which is where it is actually read.

check.reason: presence is checkable, quality is not; left to ruff's pydocstyle rules

rules.title: Use pathlib, not os.path
rules.rationale: `os.path` manipulates paths as strings, which is where separator and encoding bugs come from. `Path` carries platform semantics with it and makes the common operations obvious.

rules.title: Custom exceptions per domain
rules.statement: **Errors are typed.** Custom exceptions per domain, not `raise Exception`.
rules.rationale: `except Exception` is the only way to catch a bare `Exception`, and that clause also swallows every unrelated failure. Domain exceptions let a caller handle the case it understands and let the rest propagate.

rules.title: No print() for logging
rules.statement: No `print()` for logging — use the `logging` module.
rules.rationale: `print` writes to stdout with no level and no structure, so it cannot be filtered, routed or silenced in production — and in a CLI it corrupts the actual output the program is supposed to produce.

rules.title: No bare except
rules.statement: No bare `except:` — always catch specific exceptions.
rules.rationale: A bare except also catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit`, so it makes a program that cannot be stopped, and it hides the programming errors it was never meant to handle.

rules.title: No mutable default arguments
rules.rationale: A default is evaluated once at definition time, so the same list or dict is shared by every call. The resulting state leak between unrelated calls is one of the hardest Python bugs to see in review.

rules.title: Behaviour-describing test names
rules.rationale: pytest prints the test name and nothing else when a test fails. A name that states the expected behaviour turns that line into a bug report.

check.reason: naming quality is not mechanically decidable

rules.title: Fixtures over bare setup functions
rules.statement: Use **fixtures** (`@pytest.fixture`) for setup, not bare functions.
rules.rationale: A fixture is scoped, composable and torn down automatically. A hand-rolled setup function is none of those, and its teardown is skipped whenever a test fails early — which is exactly when cleanup matters.

check.reason: requires knowing which functions are setup

rules.title: Parametrize instead of copy-pasting tests
rules.rationale: Copy-pasted cases drift: a fix applied to one and not the others leaves a test that passes for the wrong reason. Parametrization keeps one body and names each case in the failure output.

rules.title: No sleep in tests
rules.rationale: A sleep is either too short (flaky under load) or too long (slow suite), and usually both across machines. It also hides the actual synchronisation the code needs.

rules.title: No real network or database in tests
rules.statement: No real network or DB calls — use fakes (`respx`, `responses`) or a test double.
rules.rationale: A test that reaches the network fails when the network does, passes when a remote is silently broken, and cannot run in CI without credentials. None of those outcomes tells you anything about your code.

check.reason: requires call-graph analysis to distinguish fakes from real clients

rules.title: Filesystem access stays inside tmp_path
rules.statement: No tests that depend on filesystem state outside the `tmp_path` fixture.
rules.rationale: A test writing outside its temp directory pollutes the working copy, collides with parallel runs, and can destroy real files when a path is computed wrong.

check.reason: path destinations are computed at runtime
